$comment: The exact business and legal decisions this lane CANNOT make, and which keep specific
capabilities disabled until an operator supplies them.
Nothing here is a placeholder value waiting to be filled in by code. Every entry is a
decision with a named owner. Until each is supplied through its configuration port, the
corresponding capability stays fail-closed — the software does not guess a duration, a
jurisdiction, or an approval, and does not degrade to a permissive default.
No deletion is executed by anything in this repository. There is no deletion path at all;
the retention port decides eligibility and nothing consumes that decision to delete.
raisedBy: Admin Enterprise acquisition / Shared Authority Hardening lane

decisions.question: How long may an enterprise outreach draft, and its approval receipts, be retained after creation or after a terminal state?
decisions.whyCodeCannotDecide: A retention period is a legal and commercial commitment. Inventing one would create a policy nobody approved and would silently start deleting evidence.
decisions.port: RETENTION_PORT in src/components/admin/v2/outreachRepository.mjs and retentionDecision() in functions/src/outreachAuthority.ts

decisions.owner: Founder + legal counsel + data protection owner
decisions.question: Who may delete outreach records, under what recorded authority, and is deletion hard or is it tombstoning?
decisions.whyCodeCannotDecide: Receipts are append-only audit evidence. Deleting them is a deliberate legal act, not a maintenance task.
decisions.currentBehaviour: fail-closed; NO deletion path exists in the codebase

decisions.question: Who may place and lift a legal hold, and what evidence must a hold record carry?
decisions.whyCodeCannotDecide: A hold is a legal instrument. The code can only enforce one it is told about.
decisions.currentBehaviour: three-valued: held / not held / UNKNOWN. Unknown BLOCKS. A failed read never degrades to 'not held'.
blocks: approving or transitioning a draft whose hold state cannot be determined

decisions.question: For each jurisdiction, is outreach to an unsigned course legally approved, under which wording, opt-out mechanism and policy version?
decisions.whyCodeCannotDecide: This lane is explicitly barred from authoring legal wording, opt-out language or jurisdiction policy. A default-allow would manufacture an approval nobody granted.
decisions.currentBehaviour: NO jurisdiction is approved. Every jurisdiction refuses. A truthy-but-not-true value such as 'pending' does not read as approval.
doesNotBlock: drafting, review and approval, which record an approval without transmitting anything

decisions.question: Is outbound transmission to courses authorized at all, and through which provider under which contract?
decisions.whyCodeCannotDecide: Standing instruction for this lane is that nothing is transmitted. Enabling transmission is a founder decision.
decisions.currentBehaviour: false. There is no transmitter, no mail client and no outbound HTTP in the server binding. Even a fully approved draft in an approved jurisdiction reports not sendable, with the reason transmission_not_permitted.

decisions.question: Which App Check attestation provider is configured, for which project, and when does enforcement begin?
decisions.whyCodeCannotDecide: Provisioning is a Firebase console action plus a client attestation provider. Neither exists in this repository, and claiming enforcement without them would be a fabricated production state.
decisions.currentBehaviour: not_provisioned. REQUIRED_IN_PRODUCTION is true, so the port REFUSES rather than silently allowing; commissioningReadiness() reports not ready with the operator action named.
blocks: a truthful claim that privileged callables are attested
doesNotBlock: current operation, because enforcement is not yet switched on
decisions.knownInconsistency: The Partner Portal lane already declares enforceAppCheck: true on ~59 privileged callables while the Admin lane declares it nowhere. Same project, two postures. Either App Check IS provisioned — in which case the Admin callables are unprotected — or it is not, in which case every Portal callable would reject in production. This must be resolved before either lane deploys.

decisions.question: Which existing admin_users records lack a canonical Active status, and should each be set Active or Suspended?
decisions.whyCodeCannotDecide: It requires reading production data, which this lane is barred from, and a judgement about who is genuinely still staff.
requiredValues: a completed repair pass against the generated manifest
decisions.port: scripts/admin-status-migration-dryrun.mjs (read-only; generates a plan, applies nothing)
decisions.currentBehaviour: The allowlist denies any record without a canonical Active status, including the status-less shape the previous denylist admitted. Both in-product recovery paths require an ACTIVE Director.
blocks: safe activation of the allowlist in an environment with legacy records
doesNotBlock: the change itself, which is correct; this is a data-readiness step
decisions.severity: This is the highest-risk item in the manifest: if no Director record carries a canonical Active status, there is no in-product way back in.

invariants: No duration, jurisdiction, approval or policy value is invented anywhere in this repository.
Every port above fails CLOSED while its decision is outstanding; none degrades to a permissive default.
No deletion is executed. There is no deletion path.
Unknown legal-hold state blocks. It never collapses to 'not held'.
